products.name: IMALENT MS32 Flashlight, 200,000 lumens claimed, 12 × 21700 pack, USB-C
specs: 200,000 lm (Turbo burst), stepping down to 40,000 lm
191,388 lm at turn-on, 177,957 lm at 30 s, 40,057 lm at 10 min
12 × 21700 4,000 mAh pack (4S3P), 92.2 Wh, proprietary; USB-C charging, about 3 h with the included 20 V charger; works as a power bank
Turbo about 45 s, then about 40 min at about 40,000 lm (claimed; The Gadgeteer measured 37.5 min total)
9.5 in long (242 mm), 5.9 in head (149 mm)
products.warranty: 2 years on the flashlight, 1 year on the battery and charger (IMALENT store policy)
products.returns: Refund or exchange within 30 days of receiving the goods (IMALENT store refund policy)
products.summary: The brightest flashlight in independent testing that also holds its output: 191,388 lm at turn-on and 40,057 lm after 10 minutes in 1Lumen's sphere.
products.fit: Search and rescue, large properties, farms, shorelines and anyone who needs to light a whole field for half an hour. It is not a carry light.
caveats: The 200,000 lm burst lasts about 45 seconds. The Gadgeteer measured the bezel going from 70 °F to 138 °F in about 40 seconds.
It weighs 6.83 lb, and a Budget Light Forum reviewer found the strap attachment too weak for that weight.
Rated IP56: fine in rain, not for dunking. The fans can't be serviced by the user and the battery pack is proprietary.
Battery and charger warranty is 1 year. Trustpilot reviewers of the IMALENT store report slow support on battery replacements.
Color rendering is low (about 70 CRI, per ZeroAir).
The same store listed an 'MS32 2nd grade' unit at $599.96 on 2026-11-17 without saying what '2nd grade' means. Ask before buying.

2.66 lb (1,207 g) with handle; 2.57 lb (1,164 g) without
products.warranty: 2 years on the flashlight, 1 year on the battery and charger (IMALENT store policy)
products.returns: Refund or exchange within 30 days of receiving the goods (IMALENT store refund policy)
products.summary: The longest measured throw among these high-lumen lights: 1,375 m in 1Lumen's test, farther than the MS32, in a 2.66 lb body.
products.fit: Spotting at distance: hunting fields, open water, long driveways and tree lines.
caveats: 1Lumen found its fans noisy and apparently not temperature-controlled.
Output falls to about 8,956 lm by 10 minutes, below the Acebeam X75's 21,061 lm.
Measured throw fell short of the 1,715 m claim.
No tripod mount, and the battery indicator is hard to see with the handle attached.

products.summary: The biggest burst from a pocket-size light: about 12,000 lm at turn-on in 1Lumen's test, from a 4.3 in body.
products.fit: Pocket carry for short bursts: checking a yard, a roadside or a dark lot for a few seconds.
caveats: Output drops fast: ZeroAir measured 3,835 lm at 30 seconds (29.5% of the claim), and another tester saw it settle near 1,800 lm after about 35 seconds.
The cell is proprietary, so a standard 21700 won't fit.
No moonlight mode from off, so the lowest mode is bright for night walking.
One Trustpilot buyer was quoted for a replacement head after a 3 ft drop.

notes: QUERY: 'high lumen flashlight' with brightest/most powerful variants. Top results are generic roundups (1Lumen is the only measured source), so the existing pages are thin. I couldn't check autocomplete directly (the curl call needed approval), so the variants come from search-result titles. PAIN POINTS (counts across the sources read): heat 5 (ZeroAir MS32, Gadgeteer MS32 138 °F, BLF commenter, T3/Space.com X75, 1Lumen SR16 fans); claimed vs measured output 4 (ZeroAir MS03 29.5%, BLF MS03 10,470 lm, 1Lumen SR16 throw short, ZeroAir MS08 59%); weight 4 (ZeroAir, Gadgeteer, BLF strap, Space.com 'bulky'); price 4 (BLF, Gadgeteer, ZeroAir, Space.com); proprietary battery or battery failure 4 (BLF, ZeroAir MS03, Trustpilot x2); fan noise 2 (1Lumen SR16, Space.com X75); IP rating 2 (BLF IP56, Trustpilot G35 water failure); store support: 9 negative and 7 positive of the 20 Trustpilot reviews shown (23 total). SEGMENTS: (1) maximum sustained brightness: IMALENT MS32 wins (191,388 lm turn-on, 40,057 lm at 10 min; 1Lumen). (2) a bright light to carry, waterproof, value: Acebeam X75 wins ($293.90 on acebeam.com on 2026-11-17, 1,240 g, IP68, 21,061 lm at 10 min). We don't earn from it, it's named without a link, and no Amazon record per the temporary rule. (3) throw: IMALENT SR16 has the longest measured throw on the page (1,375 m), though dedicated LEP throwers were not compared. (4) pocket burst: IMALENT MS03 (12,000 lm turn-on per 1Lumen), with the fast drop stated plainly. VERIFIED 2026-11-17: prices come from the IMALENT store home page and its Black Friday page (MS32 $749.95 with no discount; SR16 $369.95; MS03 $103.96, down from $129.95). Product URLs come from those pages' links. Warranty (2 years on the light, 1 year on the battery and charger) and the 30-day returns come from the store refund policy page. The store's product pages returned HTTP 429 every time I tried, and storecheck.py got HTTP 403. So product-page availability is inferred from the buy buttons on the Black Friday page (no sold-out labels), and specs come from independent reviews. UNVERIFIED / KEPT OFF PAGE: MS32 IP56 comes from listings and the BLF review, not the product page; the SR16 charging port is unclear (1Lumen's unit used a 19 V DC port, while a Trustpilot buyer mentions USB-C); MS18 price (one listing showed $669.95) and URL; Haikelite AK24 price, URL and weight (it is named in the text only); the X75 weight is the maker figure. The MS32 '2nd grade' listing was $599.96 and the store doesn't explain the grade. CODES: the network gave none, and the store shows automatic sale prices ('Up to 70% off') but no code.
